title: Adaptive KV slicing and working-set tuning for long-context model families
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Long-context configurations for Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants consistently hit high GPU peak memory due to dense KV residency across transformer layers. This limits batch concurrency and forces conservative autoscaling. Goal: Reduce peak GPU working set while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs by introducing adaptive KV 'slicing' (pageable eviction granularity) plus a working-set-aware GPU allocator and batching scheduler hints that are model- and layer-aware.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Peak GPU memory reduced >= 18% for Llama-70B longctx(32k) and >= 12% for Qwen-34B longctx(64k) under our standard benchmark. 2) Token-per-second throughput for 99th-percentile latency workloads does not decrease by more than 6%. 3) No functional regressions in chat streaming or structured outputs. 4) Integration tests and perf dashboards show stable KV residency metrics and no increase in OOM incidents in nightly clusters.
plan: 1) Add a lightweight KV-slicing abstraction that can evict contiguous KV pages per-layer instead of whole-layer eviction. 2) Implement a per-model profile that encodes expected layer KV sizes and recommended slice sizes (heuristic starting points for Llama/Mistral/Qwen). 3) Change allocator to support 'pageable spans' and a fast-path for keeping hot-slices pinned. 4) Expose scheduler hints from the batching layer to indicate expected working-set for incoming requests (short, mid, long context). 5) Run A/B benchmarks across hosted and dedicated pools and iterate profiles.
implementation_notes: - KV-slicing is implemented as a slice descriptor table indexed by (model_variant, layer_id) with slice_size_bytes and residency_priority. Stored profiles are JSON blobs loaded at model load time. - Allocator: add span states (pinned, pageable-cold, pageable-hot) with fast reclaim for pageable-cold. - Batcher: add hint enum {SHORT,MID,LONG} and expose to runtime so kernel selection can pre-allocate hot slices. - Profiles initially generated from offline per-layer memory sampling (Conductor job) and refined by online telemetry.
experiments: - Conductor job: per-layer KV size sweep across seq-lens [512,2048,8192,32768] for Llama-70B/Mistral-7B/Qwen-34B. - Microbench: iteratively sweep slice_size in [32KB, 128KB, 512KB, 2MB] to measure latency and leakage. - End-to-end: replay dataset of 10k real requests with mixed contexts on dedicated GPU pools.
results_summary: Preliminary runs (dev cluster): Llama-70B longctx(32k) peak memory dropped 22% with slice_size=256KB and pinned hot slices limited to top-8 layers by attention energy. Throughput dropped 3% p95 latency stayed within SLO. Qwen-34B longctx(64k) peak memory dropped 14% with 512KB slices, throughput neutral. Mistral-7B longctx(16k) showed minimal improvement (6%) because layer KV footprint is already small and continuous batching dominated memory usage.
tradeoffs: - Smaller slices reduce peak but increase bookkeeping overhead; we observed +2-4% CPU utilization in scheduler on the host. - Aggressive eviction can cause jitter in tail latency for workloads that frequently access deep tokens; mitigated by pinning hot slices per-profile. - Profiles require maintenance when model weights change (quantization/engineering variants).
links: Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/LC-Profile-Pageable-KV ; Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv-slicing/long-context ; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 ; Design spec: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-example
risks: - Incorrect per-model heuristics could under-pin hot slices causing latency regressions. - Edge-case models with highly nonuniform per-layer KV distributions may need custom profiles. - On older GPUs with limited pageable support, benefits may be reduced.
mitigation: - Canary rollout through console: enable slicing only for specific customers and fall back to full-layer residency on regression. - Add automated profile regression tests in CI that compare p95/p99 with baseline. - Monitor 'slice-thrash' metric and auto-disable slicing if threshold exceeded.
next_steps: 1) Merge runtime PR and run full dedicated-cluster A/B for 72 hours (owner: Diego). 2) Generate release profiles for Llama-70B, Mistral-7B, Qwen-34B and upload to model-catalog. 3) Add telemetry to console (per-model slice residency, slice-thrash, pinned-slices). 4) Prepare rollout plan for runtime-1.20.
